name: GeneNetWeaver
simulation_summary: Generates in silico bulk RNA expression benchmarks from GeneNetWeaver dynamical network XML/SBML models, including perturbational steady-state experiments and time-series experiments with native signed global GRN gold standards.

conditional_required.usage: Wrapper passes this GeneNetWeaver XML/SBML model to java -jar gnw-3.1.2b.jar --simulate --input-net when network_preset=custom_xml.

threading.upstream_mapping: GeneNetWeaver 3.1.2 Beta is executed through the public Java CLI. The reviewed CLI help and settings file expose no thread, worker, OpenMP, BLAS or process-count control for benchmark simulation, so ANDREA must run the wrapper with runtime_resources.threads=1.

network_preset.description: Selects the dynamical network XML used by GNW. The default uses the official sandbox InSilicoSize10-Yeast1.xml from the pinned upstream repository; custom_xml requires the gnw_dynamical_network simulator input.

network_name.description: Network root name used for normalized output identifiers and, when supported by the CLI route, upstream output filenames.

simulation_design.description: Scenario-controlled design selector. Capabilities lock this value from data_axes.experimental_design so users cannot switch the scientific design from run parameters.

solver.description: Chooses which GNW solver family supplies normalized expression.tsv. The wrapper maps ode to simulateODE=1/simulateSDE=0 and sde to simulateODE=0/simulateSDE=1, while preserving raw generated files under provenance/raw/.

expression_variant.description: Selects the GNW mRNA expression table family normalized into expression.tsv. Protein tables are preserved as native outputs but are not normalized as RNA expression.

steady_state_experiment.description: Selects which GNW steady-state perturbation family is normalized for the bulk perturbational capability. The wrapper maps this to ssKnockouts, ssKnockdowns, ssMultifactorial, ssDualKnockouts and ssDREAM4TimeSeries settings.

time_series_experiment.description: Selects which GNW time-series experiment family is normalized for the bulk time-series capability. The wrapper maps this to tsDREAM4TimeSeries, tsKnockouts, tsKnockdowns, tsMultifactorial and tsDualKnockouts settings.

maxt_ode.description: Maps to maxtSteadyStateODE, the maximum deterministic integration time before returning the current state.

maxt_sde.description: Maps to maxtSteadyStateSDE. Negative values make GNW use 1.5 times the matching ODE convergence time.

mint_sde.description: Maps to mintSDE, the minimum stochastic simulation time used to sample independent wild-type states.

num_time_series.description: Maps to numTimeSeries, the number of independent perturbation time courses generated for time-series experiment families.

maxt.description: Maps to maxtTimeSeries, the maximum measured time in each time course.

dt.description: Maps to dt, the measured time interval. GNW requires maxt to be an exact multiple of dt; the wrapper must reject incompatible values before execution.

perturbations.description: GNW perturbation generation settings. loadPerturbations is intentionally fixed to false because it requires GNW-specific sidecar files that are not part of this Phase 1 public contract.

perturbation_probability.description: Maps to perturbationProbability for DREAM4-style time-series perturbations.

time_step.description: Maps to timeStepSDE, the internal stochastic integration step size.

experimental_noise.description: GNW measurement-noise settings applied after ODE/SDE simulation.

goldstandard.description: GNW gold-standard export controls. Public truth/networks.csv always uses non-zero signed edges only.

append_zero_interactions.description: Maps to appendZeroInteractionsInGoldStandardFiles; wrapper truth normalization ignores zero rows.

parameter_bindings.description: Bulk perturbational capabilities use GNW steady-state perturbation outputs: knockouts, knockdowns, multifactorial, dual knockouts or DREAM4 perturbation steady states.

upstream_configuration: Wrapper enables exactly the selected steady-state perturbation family through ssKnockouts, ssKnockdowns, ssMultifactorial, ssDualKnockouts or ssDREAM4TimeSeries.
settings.txt outputDirectory must be an absolute /work/out/provenance/raw path; --output-path alone is not sufficient for reliable output placement.
truth_contexts.generation: The wrapper reads *_goldstandard_signed.tsv rows as source, target and sign, emits one truth/networks.csv row per signed non-self edge with context=global, and ignores zero rows from *_goldstandard.tsv.
truth_contexts.score_semantics: score is 1.0 because GNW's signed gold-standard file stores topology and sign but not edge magnitudes; sign is copied from the native '+' or '-' field.
limitations: The public GRN is fixed for the whole dataset and does not vary by perturbation column.
Kinetic parameters in the XML drive expression but are not exported as public edge magnitudes.
Autoregulatory interactions are excluded by default through GNW settings.

truth_contexts.explanation: GNW steady-state perturbation outputs do not define groups of expression columns with distinct regulatory networks; duplicating the global GRN by perturbation family would not be native or biologically distinct group truth.
Each perturbation column is simulated from the same fixed GNW dynamical network, and GNW does not emit perturbation-specific GRN rewiring.

derivations.method: For systematic knockout and knockdown tables, infer one direct intervention per expression column from column order and gene identifiers. For multifactorial, DREAM4 and dual-knockout outputs, parse the upstream perturbation sidecar files and align rows to normalized expression columns. Write extras/perturbation_design.tsv with one row per expression column.
assumptions: GNW file naming and row order follow the public DREAM benchmark conventions produced by BenchmarkGeneratorDream4.
The selected expression table and perturbation sidecars are generated in the same run from the same settings.
limitations: Systematic knockout and knockdown interventions are implicit in GNW output shape rather than emitted as a separate sidecar file.
Different steady-state experiment families use different upstream perturbation encodings, so Phase 2 must test each supported family.

derivations.method: Collapse distinct intervention definitions from perturbation_design into extras/interventions.tsv, preserving perturbed gene IDs, intervention type and signed effect when available.
assumptions: Perturbation columns with the same intervention metadata represent the same intervention class.
limitations: GNW perturbation strengths are not always comparable across knockout, knockdown, drug-like and multifactorial families.

derivations.method: Write every normalized expression gene identifier to extras/enrichment_background.txt, one gene per line.
assumptions: The simulated expression row universe is the appropriate synthetic background for downstream enrichment workflows.
limitations: No organism-specific functional annotation universe is simulated.

derivations.method: Write the same signed non-self edges used for global truth into extras/prior_grn.tsv with source, target, score and sign.
assumptions: The simulator gold standard may be useful as an oracle prior only when explicitly requested.
limitations: This is truth-derived, not an independent noisy prior.

derivations.method: Write unique source genes from signed non-self global truth edges to extras/tf_list.txt, one gene per line.
assumptions: Genes with outgoing simulated regulatory edges define the synthetic regulator universe.
limitations: The list is simulator-derived and not an organism-specific TF catalogue.

native_outputs.description: Native GNW *_goldstandard.tsv file, optionally including zero interactions.
Raw GNW mRNA and protein expression tables for selected solver/noise variants.
Raw GNW perturbation sidecar tables such as multifactorial perturbations, DREAM4 time-series perturbations and dual-knockout indexes.
The GNW XML/SBML dynamical model copied or regenerated for the run.
Native GNW normalization constant file when GNW writes normalized noisy outputs.

artifacts_aux.description: Resolved GNW settings.txt used for the Java CLI run.
Captured stdout/stderr from the GNW Java process.
Java version, GNW jar version and pinned upstream commit.
Mappings from native GNW gene and experiment identifiers to normalized public IDs.

parameter_bindings.description: Bulk time-series capabilities use GNW time-series outputs and lock the run to ts* settings rather than steady-state ss* settings.

upstream_configuration: Wrapper enables exactly the selected time-series family through tsDREAM4TimeSeries, tsKnockouts, tsKnockdowns, tsMultifactorial or tsDualKnockouts.
time_series.maxt must be an exact multiple of time_series.dt because GNW validates maxtTimeSeries/dt before simulation.
truth_contexts.generation: The wrapper reads *_goldstandard_signed.tsv rows as source, target and sign, emits one truth/networks.csv row per signed non-self edge with context=global, and ignores zero rows from *_goldstandard.tsv.
truth_contexts.score_semantics: score is 1.0 because GNW's signed gold-standard file stores topology and sign but not edge magnitudes; sign is copied from the native '+' or '-' field.
limitations: The GRN is fixed across the whole time course.
GNW time-series outputs do not model timepoint-specific network rewiring.
Kinetic parameters in the XML drive dynamics but are not exported as public truth edge magnitudes.

truth_contexts.explanation: GNW time-series outputs do not emit groups of timepoint columns with distinct regulatory networks.
Expression columns are timepoint observations generated from one fixed GNW dynamical network; no timepoint-specific GRNs are emitted.

derivations.method: Parse each GNW time-series block, assign one normalized column per measured row, and write extras/timepoints.tsv with column_id, timepoint and series_id aligned to expression.tsv column order.
assumptions: The native time column in each GNW time-series table is the public time coordinate.
limitations: Multiple GNW time courses share time values but represent different perturbation trajectories; series_id is required to disambiguate them.

derivations.method: Align each time-series block and timepoint row to its upstream perturbation vector, then write one perturbation_design row per normalized expression column.
assumptions: GNW writes perturbation sidecars in the same series order as the time-series expression blocks.
limitations: A perturbation applies to a whole time course; repeated rows across timepoints are wrapper-derived column annotations.

derivations.method: Collapse distinct intervention definitions from perturbation_design into extras/interventions.tsv, preserving perturbed gene IDs, intervention type and signed effect when available.
assumptions: Timepoint columns from the same series share the same direct intervention definition.
limitations: The intervention table describes experiment-level perturbations, not dynamic causal effects at individual timepoints.

derivations.method: Write every normalized expression gene identifier to extras/enrichment_background.txt, one gene per line.
assumptions: The simulated expression row universe is the appropriate synthetic background for downstream enrichment workflows.
limitations: No organism-specific functional annotation universe is simulated.

derivations.method: Write the same signed non-self edges used for global truth into extras/prior_grn.tsv with source, target, score and sign.
assumptions: The simulator gold standard may be useful as an oracle prior only when explicitly requested.
limitations: This is truth-derived, not an independent noisy prior.

derivations.method: Write unique source genes from signed non-self global truth edges to extras/tf_list.txt, one gene per line.
assumptions: Genes with outgoing simulated regulatory edges define the synthetic regulator universe.
limitations: The list is simulator-derived and not an organism-specific TF catalogue.
